analysis.title: US Market Intelligence Morning Briefing (October 15, 2026)
key_insights: Treasuries sold off hard at 8:30am ET on Oct 14 after the hotter-than-expected September core CPI, then recovered nearly 15bp during the day. The 2Y ended more than 15bp below its morning high. JPM saw no clear catalyst or dovish signal behind the reversal.

JPM gives three reasons for the yield reversal: wait for PPI and Fedspeak before reading a Fed signal into yields, the market overreacted when October hike odds jumped above 50% (now ~32%, with ~30bp of hikes priced through year-end), and there were signs of a move into quality and safe assets along with concern about a possible AI-related credit event.

SOXX fell for a seventh straight day, with financing risks and IPO timelines at the center of the AI story. JPM thinks memories of the July selloff played a part, with investors possibly de-grossing ahead of IPO-related updates.

Positioning Intel: US positioning largely unchanged month to date, with TPM at a neutral ~46th percentile versus ~19th percentile near the late-July low. JPM sees potential for further de-grossing into key tech catalysts but stays constructive on the sector and sees a possible dip-buying opportunity.

JPM's US Market Intel view is Tactically Bullish into earnings. SOX is ~20% off its July lows and ~15% below its June all-time highs, which JPM says points to an inflection. Recent Hynix and Samsung updates are cited as evidence of ongoing thematic strength, and JPM expects breadth to reverse into and out of earnings season.

FX Sales (Steve Bruner) says CPI strength was narrower in breadth than the headline suggests, driven partly by elevated shelter numbers and one-offs like tuition. He sees equity-led rate trading and tech-related demand destruction (SOX -4%, SNOW -6.3%, hyperscaler index -3.1%) but his instinct is that rates have not yet crossed the AI Rubicon. A 2% rather than 4% growth rate does not by itself kill structural inflation.

JPM initial CPI read: unrounded core CPI MoM was 0.335% versus Street 0.2% and Feroli's 0.18%, driving an 11-16bp 2Y spike. OIS pricing showed 50% probability of an October hike with one hike in December as base case, keeping 2027 hike odds elevated. The increase was broad across categories, and Chase card data and bank earnings point to resilient consumer spending.

JPM Econ (Abiel Reinhart) forecasts core PCE at 0.31% m/m (3.1% y/y, 2.8% 3m saar), enough to put the October FOMC in play, though the base case remains a December hike. Core goods rose 0.25% and core services 0.37%, supercore rose 0.42%, and headline CPI beat swap pricing by over 7bp, the largest upside surprise since March 2024.

ETF desk flows (Jonathan Rogerson): customers are buying energy (MLPA, MLPX, AMLP, IEO) and growth (large IWF block lifted, offers wanted in VUG and VONG), and opportunistically buying DRAM after the pullback. International products are seeing supply (EEM, IEMG near redemption bands, a large EFA block sold, continued supply in EWJ and FLJP), and the desk expects that to extend after the CPI print.

PPI and Retail Sales preview: Feroli sees headline PPI +0.5% MoM (5.3% YoY), core PPI +0.3% MoM (4.4% YoY), Food PPI +0.7%, Retail Sales headline +0.4% MoM and control group +0.2%, both driven by Chase card data.

Overnight and pre-market: sentiment on AI themes is bearish after TSMC's Q4 sales guide and AI commentary was solid but margin softness and cautious non-AI demand chatter weighed. Pre-market NVDA -1.8%, AMZN -1.6%, AAPL +0.8%. Bonds bull flattened with yields down ~7-11bp, and DXY slid ~58bp to ~101.98.

Europe/UK: yields are lower globally (10y Bunds -10bp, Gilts -9bp). Staples, Health Care and Telecom outperform while Semis, Basic Resources and Energy lag. UKX +0.5%, SX5E -0.6%, SXXP -0.1%, DAX -0.3%.

Monetization Menu (Oct 12) is relatively unchanged, preferring Tech and some Cyclicals with the AI theme globally bullish. JPM would focus the COVID Reopening theme on Cruise Lines, Hotels and Retailers given consumer strength and relative insulation from high energy prices. Ex-AI internationally, JPM likes Brazil and Japan.

Older Monetization Menu (Oct 5, Sep 28, Sep 21): still long Tech but no longer paired with an RTY short because of squeeze risk from lower oil or yields. Software is gaining traction as a non-consensus bullish play, and Banks are favored ex-AI. A US/Iran deal is the biggest catalyst, which would squeeze EU and RTY higher. JPM maintains +Tech vs -RTY with a Mag7, Memory and Semis mix, and likes Brazil and Latam irrespective of the AI view.

Stated risks: momentum/tech unwind, tech earnings miss, AI credit fears and spread widening, a spike in bond or equity vol, weaker consumer data. Catalysts: CPI Oct 14, Retail Sales and PPI Oct 15, Flash PMIs Oct 23, Fed day Oct 28, and bank earnings to restart the Cyclicals trade.

earnings_insights: Bank earnings from the prior day (Oct 14) are cited, with Chase card data, as showing elevated consumer demand and spending despite inflationary pressures. No figures are given.
US earnings today (Oct 15): AA, BNY, IBKR, JBHT, MRSH, PLD, PNC, SCHW, USB. JPM expects bank earnings with a favorable consumer and lending outlook to help restart the Cyclicals trade.

Hynix and Samsung recent earnings updates are cited as pointing to ongoing thematic strength in Semis. TSMC's Q4 sales guide and AI commentary were described as solid, with margin softness and cautious non-AI demand chatter. No figures are given.

tension_points.bull_case: JPM stays Tactically Bullish: SOX is ~20% off July lows and ~15% below June ATHs, Hynix and Samsung updates point to ongoing thematic strength, and positioning at the ~46th percentile leaves room for a dip-buying opportunity.

tension_points.what_invalidates: A tech earnings miss or AI credit fears with spread widening, which JPM lists among its risks.

tension_points.bull_case: Dovish remarks from Bowman, Williams and Jefferson suggest a more patient Committee, the hike odds overreaction has faded to ~32% for October, and JPM sees a case for lower yields if dovish inflation prints remove hike expectations.

tension_points.what_invalidates: Today's PPI and Retail Sales prints (Oct 15, 8:30am ET), and the heavy run of Fedspeak.
